Key implementation and tests for docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md:
1) Core deep-validation rule implementation - File: src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts - Header explicitly ties rule to this story and its deep-validation requirements: - "@story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md" - "@req REQ-DEEP-PARSE - Parse comments and extract story/requirement metadata" - "@req REQ-DEEP-MATCH - Match @req annotations to story file requirements" - "@req REQ-DEEP-CACHE - Cache requirement IDs per story file for efficient validation" - "@req REQ-DEEP-PATH - Validate and resolve story file paths safely" - Deep parsing and requirement extraction (REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-FORMAT, REQ-DEEP-SECTION): - loadAndCacheRequirements(...) reads the referenced story file and extracts requirement IDs with: - const regex = /REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+/g; - Loops regex.exec(content) and adds each match to a Set. - Because it scans the entire markdown text, it supports IDs in different sections and formats: - Bold identifiers in story requirements sections, e.g. docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md: - "- **REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE**: ESLint plugin follows standard Node.js module structure" - Bullet list requirements in fixtures: - tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md: "- REQ-BULLET-LIST - a requirement in bullet list format" - tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md, story_multi_b.md with "- REQ-SHARED-ID", "- REQ-ONLY-A", "- REQ-ONLY-B". - Requirement matching and reporting (REQ-DEEP-MATCH, REQ-DEEP-ERROR + UX AC): - extractReqIdFromLine(line) parses @req lines: returns parts[1] as requirement ID. - validateReqLine(...) resolves the story and requirement set via resolveStoryAndRequirements(...), then calls checkRequirementExists(...). - checkRequirementExists(...) reports an error if the referenced requirement is missing: - context.report({ messageId: "reqMissing", data: { reqId, storyPath } }). - meta.messages defines clear error text: - reqMissing: "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'". - Path validation and caching (REQ-DEEP-PATH, REQ-DEEP-CACHE): - validateAndResolveStoryPath(...) enforces security on storyPath: - Rejects traversal or absolute paths; reports messageId: "invalidPath" with storyPath. - Resolves storyPath using path.resolve(cwd, storyPath) and ensures it stays under cwd. - loadAndCacheRequirements(...) uses a Map<string, Set> reqCache per resolved story path: - Only reads and parses each story file once per run, satisfying caching requirement. - resolveStoryAndRequirements(...) wires validation and caching together and returns { resolvedStoryPath, reqSet }. - Error handling for file issues (Error Handling AC): - loadAndCacheRequirements(...) is wrapped in try/catch: - On read error, it stores an empty Set in the cache, preventing rule crashes. - Missing or unreadable files result in missing-req errors rather than exceptions, which is graceful behavior within ESLint runs. - Integration with annotation parsing and ESLint lifecycle (Integration AC): - extractStoryPath(comment) parses @story lines from JSDoc-style comments. - handleAnnotationLine(...) dispatches based on prefix: - @story → updates storyPath (via extractStoryPath). - @req → calls validateReqLine(...). - @implements → calls validateImplementsLine(...). - processAllComments(...) obtains comments from context.getSourceCode().getAllComments() and processes them with shared cache and storyPath. - programListener(context) encapsulates this logic and is registered via create(context) → { Program: programListener(context) }. - src/index.ts includes "valid-req-reference" in RULE_NAMES and TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES, and thus in the exported configs, so it runs alongside existing file-validation and annotation rules.
2) Tests directly tied to this story - File: tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts - Header: - "Tests for: docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md" - "@story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md" - "@req REQ-DEEP-PARSE - Verify valid-req-reference rule enforces existing requirement content" - Uses ESLint RuleTester to verify behavior. - Valid cases (prove correct deep validation on multiple formats and structures): 1) name: "[REQ-DEEP-PARSE] valid requirement reference existing in story file" - code: // @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md // @req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE - docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md contains **REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE** (confirmed by search), so no errors expected. 2) name: "[REQ-DEEP-BULLET] valid bullet list requirement existing in bullet story fixture" - code: // @story tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md // @req REQ-BULLET-LIST - tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md defines "- REQ-BULLET-LIST - a requirement in bullet list format", showing bullet-format support. 3) and 4) Valid @implements usage with multi-story fixtures (REQ-SHARED-ID, REQ-ONLY-A/B) from tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md and story_multi_b.md, confirming multi-story and repeated-ID handling. - Invalid cases (prove error messaging and path handling): 1) name: "[REQ-DEEP-MATCH] missing requirement in story file" - code uses story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md and non-existent REQ-NON-EXISTENT. - Expects errors: [{ messageId: "reqMissing", data: { reqId: "REQ-NON-EXISTENT", storyPath: "docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md" } }]. 2) and 3) Path traversal and absolute-path invalidation for @story: - Use "../docs/stories/..." and "/absolute/path/..."; each expects messageId: "invalidPath" with the offending storyPath. 4) name: "[REQ-DEEP-BULLET] missing bullet list requirement in bullet story fixture" - code references REQ-MISSING-BULLET in tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md. - Expects reqMissing with reqId: "REQ-MISSING-BULLET" and storyPath: "tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md". 5) and 6) @implements with missing requirement and path traversal, each expecting reqMissing or invalidPath respectively. - These tests explicitly exercise: core functionality, multiple requirement formats (plain, bullet, multi-story), integration with ESLint, and clear error messages.
3) Documentation of deep requirement validation behavior (Documentation AC) - File: docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md - Top section explicitly references this story and requirements: - "@story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md" - "@req REQ-DEEP-PARSE - Parse story files to extract requirement identifiers" - "@req REQ-DEEP-MATCH - Validate `@req` references against story file content" - "@req REQ-DEEP-PATH - Protect against path traversal in story paths" - Describes behavior in detail: - Confirms rule parses every referenced story file to extract requirement IDs. - States it validates each @req/@implements requirement ID against those IDs. - Documents error types: invalidPath and reqMissing, and when they occur. - Provides concrete examples of correct and incorrect usage, including different formats and multi-story `@implements` scenarios, satisfying the story’s documentation acceptance criterion.
4) Evidence that story requirements are referenced and implemented - Searching for REQ-DEEP-*: - src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts contains multiple references to: - REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-MATCH, REQ-DEEP-CACHE, REQ-DEEP-PATH in JSDoc tags on functions implementing parsing, matching, caching, and path validation. - tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts uses requirement IDs in test names and file header. - docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md defines REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-MATCH, REQ-DEEP-FORMAT, REQ-DEEP-SECTION, REQ-DEEP-CACHE, REQ-DEEP-ERROR. - Additional related fixtures: - tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md, story_multi_a.md, story_multi_b.md provide concrete markdown structures that the regex-based parser successfully handles.
Given this evidence, the ESLint rule valid-req-reference, its tests, and documentation collectively implement deep requirement content validation exactly as specified in Story 010.0, and they are integrated into the plugin’s rule set.
traceability.notes: The deep validation story (010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION) is fully implemented. The valid-req-reference rule reads referenced story files, extracts requirement IDs using a flexible regex, caches results, and verifies that each @req and @implements requirement ID exists in the corresponding story file. It provides clear, specific error messages (reqMissing and invalidPath), gracefully handles invalid paths and file read issues without crashing ESLint, and integrates with existing annotation and file-validation logic via the plugin’s rule registration and configs. Tests in tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts explicitly reference this story and thoroughly cover valid and invalid scenarios across multiple requirement formats and story file structures. Documentation in docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md explains the behavior with concrete examples. All acceptance criteria in the story are met, so the status is PASSED.
